title: A Blocker-Tolerant mm-Wave Low-Noise Amplifier Utilizing Doherty Active Load Modulation for Linearity Enhancement
problem: Emerging mm-wave applications (massive MIMO, automotive radar, SATCOM-on-the-Move, AR/VR) require high-linearity receivers/LNAs to handle multiple concurrent signals or weak signals amid strong interferers. Conventional LNA designs optimize for noise at weak signals but cannot maintain linearity with strong blockers.
motivation: Future mm-wave wireless links operate in complex electromagnetic environments with unknown strong interferences; linearity becomes a critical design metric alongside noise figure, requiring architectures beyond conventional low-noise-first approaches.
method: Blocker-tolerant mm-wave LNA leveraging Doherty active load modulation to enhance linearity across wide input power range. Doherty architecture dynamically adjusts gain vs. linearity trade-off, maintaining output power efficiency under strong blockers.
key_novelty: Doherty active load modulation applied to mm-wave LNA design enabling simultaneous high linearity and low noise in presence of strong interferers.
contributions: mm-Wave LNA with superior linearity enhancement via Doherty active load modulation
Blocker-tolerant design handling strong interferers with varying angles of arrival
Maintains low noise figure while supporting dynamic input power range
primary_theme: Doherty-modulated mm-wave LNA for blocker tolerance
